## Native ordering and lifecycle

Eleven independent assertions against freshly extracted pinned bytecode passed ([receipt](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/bsl-prefix-sustained-r8/review/native-order-checks.json)). `ShaderChunkRenderer.begin` binds the real `GlProgram` before interface setup; `DefaultChunkRenderer.render` performs the whole chunk draw loop between begin/end; end resets the interface before unbinding. `SodiumShader.updateUniforms` runs sampler update, native uniform update, then real custom-uniform push. `ProgramUniforms.update` always executes the DYNAMIC stage before frame/tick gates, detaches the preceding owner's listeners and installs the current owner. Thus repeated same-frame setups are not suppressed by a per-frame cache. Reset's HEAD injection precedes native listener detachment. Actual application of these Mixins remains unexecuted.

R8 gives each owner and each of its seven uniforms a separate listener signal. Active is last in registration and dispatch. Retirement disables/invalidates before firing. Dispatch checks render-thread status, recorded bound owner and actual `GL_CURRENT_PROGRAM`; it cannot intentionally update a foreign bound program. Begin/reset/restore do not revive retired image proof. `BslPrefixEpochR8` uses exact token identity, monotonic generations and one-shot install; returning to prior context objects cannot restore a stale token. Native mutation generation also fences capture before the normal object has been discovered. World, resources, pack, normal, format and pipeline identity are retained. Unknown/new owners beyond the finite four-owner bound use default Active0.

The pinned NORMAL format path is consistent: `LabPBRTextureFormat.canInterpolateValues(NORMAL)` returns true, and the inherited `TextureFormat.setupTextureParameters` immediately skips parameter writes in that case. R8 checks exact format class/identity and NORMAL interpolation, wraps both actual format invocations before they execute, then refreshes Active after `onSetShaderTexture` returns. Pinned pipeline bytecode puts NORMAL and SPECULAR setup before PBR notification. Changed/unknown formats retire the captured proof before native setup.

## Foreign-thread reload boundary

The disclosed CPU/GPU timing distinction is real: `BslPrefixSustainedR8.Owner.retire/fire` can retire CPU proof on a foreign thread without changing a still-bound GPU Active1. A reload initiated between setup and draw can therefore leave the **uniform** stale until reset or next setup. This alone is not a counterexample to the sampled-image upper bound: closing/replacing resource-manager CPU data does not itself change the captured GL pixels.

Checked the concrete native storage paths rather than treating this as a demonstrated unsafe draw. `TextureUtil.prepareImage` asserts render-thread-or-init; PBR atlas allocation invokes it. `NativeImage.upload` queues foreign-thread uploads as `RenderCall`s and asserts the render lane in `_upload`. TextureManager's reload executor queues its application through `recordRenderCall`. `RenderSystem.flipFrame` replays that queue before swap. The inspected chunk draw loop has no queue replay. A normal native mutation on the render lane reaches R8's HEAD retirement before mutation; a later setup recomputes Active from the permanently retired CPU state. No changed-image/old-Active consuming draw was established in these pinned paths.

This supports a finite private run under the current native classes and their normal render-loop scheduling. It does not certify arbitrary mods that replay queues during chunk drawing, external/raw GL image or sampler writes, or foreign-thread native misuse. Actual injected reload/upload/filter/reset events and the next owner setup/draw have not been observed. Root's finite runtime check should record those thread/program/order joins; if it sees changed pixels or sampler state consumed under Active1, that is the concrete unsafe gap to fix. General shipping certification is outside this review.
